use_case.name: Maintenance Fault Reporting via Finnish Voice
use_case.description: Field technicians report facility faults via Finnish voice messages; the system transcribes, extracts a structured maintenance ticket, validates it, and presents it to a supervisor for approval before entry into the maintenance system.

business_spec.current_process: Field technicians manually enter fault information (what is broken, where it is, urgency) into the maintenance system using a computer or mobile form.
pain_points: Manual entry is slow, especially in the field
Details are frequently omitted or incorrectly recorded
No structured validation before tickets reach the maintenance system
business_spec.proposed_solution: An AI workflow that accepts a Finnish voice message from a technician, transcribes it, extracts a structured maintenance ticket, validates the extraction, and routes the ticket to a supervisor for approval before it is entered into the maintenance system.
input_artifacts: Finnish voice message recorded by the field technician via mobile app
target_outputs: Structured maintenance ticket (JSON) approved by supervisor
success_criteria: Faster incident reporting with fewer missing details
Supervisor can verify and approve each ticket before it enters the maintenance system
expected_value: Reduced manual data entry time for technicians
Fewer missing or incorrect details in maintenance tickets
Faster fault response through structured, supervisor-approved tickets
risks: Finnish transcription errors in noisy field environments
Incorrect asset, location, fault, or urgency values extracted
Unsupported enumeration values introduced by the model
Ticket transferred to the maintenance system without supervisor approval
business_spec.poc_goal: Accept a supplied Finnish audio fixture, exit successfully, produce a non-empty parseable JSON maintenance ticket, preserve the fixture facts, include all required fields (location, fault_description, urgency), and leave unsupported or unknown values null rather than inventing them.

security_constraints: Raw audio must not be retained after transcription
Approved ticket and supervisor approval decision may be retained
Authentication, RBAC, and full audit-log implementation are out of scope for PoC

evaluation_requirements.threshold: no numerical threshold specified for single-fixture PoC

field_descriptions.reporter_name: Name of the technician who recorded the message (optional; extracted if stated).
field_descriptions.asset_identifier: Identifier of the asset or equipment that is faulty (optional; extracted if stated).
field_descriptions.location: Location of the fault within the facility (required; e.g. building, floor, room).
field_descriptions.fault_description: Description of what is broken or malfunctioning (required; verbatim from report).
field_descriptions.urgency: Urgency level of the fault (required; one of: low, medium, high).
field_descriptions.observation_date: Date the fault was observed in YYYY-MM-DD format (optional).
field_descriptions.observation_time: Time the fault was observed in HH:MM format (optional).
field_descriptions.actions_taken: Any immediate actions the technician already took before reporting (optional; list of strings).
field_descriptions.uncertain_fields: Names of fields whose values could not be reliably extracted or are missing (for required fields: must be listed here when null).

target_output_spec.missing_value_policy: Set the field to null and add the field name to uncertain_fields. Do not invent or guess values. Required fields (location, fault_description, urgency) must appear in uncertain_fields when null.
validation_rules: urgency must be one of: low, medium, high — never any other string
observation_date must be YYYY-MM-DD format when present
observation_time must be HH:MM format when present
required fields (location, fault_description, urgency) must be present in the JSON; a null value is acceptable only when the field name is also listed in uncertain_fields

assumptions.text: Audio recordings are submitted in WAV, MP3, or M4A format via the mobile app.
Risks were explicitly identified by the user; no additional risk assessment is required for the PoC.
No additional stakeholders beyond field technicians and supervisor are required for the PoC.
Integration with the maintenance system is out of scope for the PoC; the approved JSON ticket is the final output.
The personal data flag is set to 'yes' because audio may contain technician names and internal facility details.
LLMJudge uses azure_openai provider (same as extractor). A different provider would reduce shared-model bias, but no second provider is configured for this PoC.

selected_modules.name: AudioToStructuredData
selected_modules.reason: Input is Finnish audio; module encapsulates transcription, Finnish enhancement, and structured extraction in a single pipeline. enhanced_transcript=True is set because language is Finnish.

steps.name: Transcribe, enhance and extract maintenance ticket
Supervisor reviews ticket, transcript and validation report

exceptions.name: Ticket returned for correction and resubmission

traceability.required_by: technical_spec.language=fi; subsumed by AudioToStructuredData — not a separate step
technical_spec.human_review=yes; pre-screens extraction before supervisor review
